answer: Give every identity a surprise oral exam. Each epoch the beacon picks one of its past answers and a random stranger, who asks a follow-up about one detail: why that number, what breaks first. The reply must arrive within minutes and stay consistent with the original, so an identity has to carry its own reasoning like a pearl it can turn over. A farm that pasted one text across a thousand heads must defend a thousand answers live, each with its own model call and memory. Thin answers crumble like shale; real ones hold like a bridge.
